stem: A nurse educator explains the difference between a preceptor and a mentor. Which description best fits a preceptor?

options.A: A long-term career adviser who supports professional development but does not participate in clinical orientation or competency feedback.
options.B: An experienced, competent nurse who serves as a role model and resource, coaches the new nurse into the role, evaluates performance, and provides feedback for improvement.
options.C: A disciplinary manager whose primary function is enforcing attendance and employment rules rather than coaching transition into the clinical role.
options.D: A peer selected only for social support who does not observe clinical practice, evaluate performance, or provide role-specific feedback.

rationale: Open RN describes preceptors as experienced and competent nurses who serve as role models and resources to newly hired nurses, coach them into the nursing role, answer questions, evaluate performance, and provide feedback for improvement. B directly matches this description.
educational_objective: Differentiate the preceptor role from mentorship by recognizing the preceptor’s structured role in clinical transition, coaching, evaluation, and feedback.
source_organization: NCBI Bookshelf / Open Resources for Nursing (Open RN)

source_claim_supported: A nursing preceptor is an experienced competent nurse who supports transition into practice through role modeling, coaching, performance evaluation, and feedback.

source_original.stem: A nurse educator explains the difference between a preceptor and a mentor. Which description best fits a preceptor?

options.A: A long-term informal career adviser who supports professional development but does not participate in clinical orientation or competency evaluation.
options.B: An experienced clinician who provides structured role-specific orientation, coaching, feedback, and performance evaluation during transition into practice.
options.C: A disciplinary manager whose primary function is enforcing attendance and employment rules rather than coaching transition into the clinical role.
options.D: A peer selected for social support who does not observe clinical practice, evaluate performance, or provide role-specific feedback.

source_original.rationale: Open RN describes preceptors as experienced nurses who serve as role models and resources, coach the new nurse into the role, evaluate performance, and provide feedback during transition into practice.

correction_summary: Retained the preceptor-versus-mentor construct and key B, rewrote B to mirror the exact Open RN description, and preserved easy difficulty.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Preceptor role in nursing transition to practice
audit_findings.source_authority: NCBI/Open RN nursing management text; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.exact_locator: Preparation for the RN Role > preceptor description
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final keyed option directly reproduces the source-defined functions of the preceptor and does not blur the role into general mentorship or disciplinary management.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because it describes a mentor-like long-term development role and excludes clinical transition functions.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because disciplinary employment enforcement is not the defining preceptor role.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because preceptors do observe, evaluate, coach, and give feedback.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B contains the defining transition-to-practice functions.
audit_findings.cueing: All options describe possible support roles and are comparable in specificity.
audit_findings.blueprint: Management of Care — supervision, resources, role development and care delivery.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read the Open RN preceptor section, mentor discussion, all options, rationale and NCSBN mapping. B remained uniquely correct.
